### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via directSignIn (literal, a string literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_QUERY_PARAMS; a string literal in runDirectSignIn))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_QUERY_PARAMS; a string literal in runDirectSignIn), directSignIn (literal, a string literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER), /api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct (route, a path literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via callbackURL (literal, a string literal in DIRECT_SIGN_IN_QUERY_PARAMS; a string literal in runDirectSignIn))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct (route, a path literal in AUTH_ROUTE_LEDGER))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json de395b428dfb58bad404e1ab67b1db01a93fa4c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `06f0dc6c10fdfe4e41e8753eda3e84b402955241` — the merge of head `0cb06990f2f5280486d69280f505fcd64aa59691` into base `de395b428dfb58bad404e1ab67b1db01a93fa4c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 06f0dc6c10fdfe4e41e8753eda3e84b402955241 && git checkout 06f0dc6c10fdfe4e41e8753eda3e84b402955241
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin de395b428dfb58bad404e1ab67b1db01a93fa4c0 0cb06990f2f5280486d69280f505fcd64aa59691 && git checkout -B drift-repro de395b428dfb58bad404e1ab67b1db01a93fa4c0 && git merge --no-ff 0cb06990f2f5280486d69280f505fcd64aa59691

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json de395b428dfb58bad404e1ab67b1db01a93fa4c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs de395b428dfb58bad404e1ab67b1db01a93fa4c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-A) at head `0cb06990f2f5280486d69280f505fcd64aa59691`, read 2026-11-19T16:52Z.

Checklist (`l1-review-checklist.md`), read on GitHub and in the head tree, not from the report:

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`. The only closing keyword is `Fixes #35474`, which fits: the card is delivered whole. No other issue number appears in the body.
- **Scope.** 5 files, +78/−8, all inside the claim's declared file surface (claim 7014000854). No `content/docs/releases/` edit. `packages/spec/**` is untouched.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` patch. Both declaration lines sit at line start in the changeset and the PR body. `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- **The point d7-A asked me to judge: `Clause-②: no`.** I accept the claim's reading, under `execution-duties.md`'s rule that removing a mis-refusal the published contract text already negates is `no`, provided the `no` cites that text. The cite fits:
  - The `afterSignOut` describe in `packages/spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts` promises that `identity-provider` "sends it back through GET /auth/sign-in/direct, so the identity provider shows its own sign-in page".
  - `/sign-out` already takes a body `state` (`sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts` `SignOutBody`) and forwards it to the end-session URL (`oidcEndSessionUrl`, `searchParams.set('state', …)`). Per RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §3, the provider echoes it onto the redirect.
  - A `400` on that echo therefore contradicts the published promise.
  - The old refusal was the door's generic closed-set guard (route rule 5), not a deliberate refusal of `state`. No test on main pins `state` as refused, so this is not a ruling guard, security refusal or fail-closed being removed.
  - It is also not a runtime security-boundary change. The door is public and mints nothing, and anyone could already `GET` it without `state` and get the same `302`. The value is never read, compared or forwarded, which the pins assert. The platform does not mint the sign-out `state` itself (it forwards a client-supplied one), so the door has nothing to verify it against.
  - No new route, no new export name. `DIRECT_SIGN_IN_QUERY_PARAMS` keeps its `readonly string[]` type. Route rule 5 still holds: every other name is refused, and the CONTROL pin shows it.
- **Code.** In the refusal block, `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage(...) ?? repeated…` keeps the unknown-name sentence ahead of the repeated one. `repeated` walks the declared set in order, so a repeated `callbackURL` still answers the same sentence as before. `directSignInNetworkRefusal` reads only `callbackURL`, so it is unaffected.
- **Tests.** Four pins in the shared-harness file, which is the right home under AGENTS.md.
  - The refusal pins assert `status` 400 and `error.code` `VALIDATION_ERROR` (the full error object on the repeated case).
  - The positive pins assert a byte-equal vendor start body, a `302` to the IdP authorize, and that the echoed value appears nowhere in it.
  - Positive control: ablating back to `['callbackURL']` turns the three state pins red while CONTROL stays green, and the restore was verified blob-equal.
- **Prose checked against the diff.**
  - Changeset: "the door answered `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` instead of showing the identity provider's sign-in page" (true on main, unknown-name path); "accepts one `state` and ignores it … starts a new sign-in with its own state" (pins 1 and 2); "A `state` sent twice is still refused `400`" (pin 3); "any other unknown query parameter is refused as before" (CONTROL); "The shipped Console sends no `state`" (`ui/packages/auth/src/createAuthClient.ts` `signOut` sends `{ callbackURL }` only).
  - `sso.mdx`: "accepted once and ignored, since the door starts a new sign-in with its own" is true.
  - No other copy of the door's query set exists in `content/docs` or the plugin.
- **Gates.** CI at `0cb06990`: 55 check runs, every one `success` or `skipped`, including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and `Build Docs` (all `success`). The three locally NOT-MEASURED families are named with their reasons and are covered by CI.
- **Accepted deviations.** The branch is `claude/project-thread-aru6wr`, the declared platform exception in the claim. The pins went into the shared harness file instead of a new file.
- **Nit, no change owed.** The ledger note says "as the post-logout return under afterSignOut identity-provider it accepts one state". The door accepts one `state` whatever `afterSignOut` reads; the clause names why it is there, not a condition. Harmless.
- **Contract review.** None owed. There is no `Clause-②: yes`, no narrowing, no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path. `.changeset` and `content/docs` are prose faces, checked sentence by sentence above.
- **Out of scope / filings.** None.
